[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Day and Night: Conversations with Sapphic Desire — Rebekah Cranes (cranes-day-and-night). The verses the casting arrives at (unit 34–unit 36):

Day and Night 34

> *Sappho 44b*
>
> The Muses' shining
>
> gifts make the Charites
>
> slender: don't forget the anger
>
> that mortals share

Day and Night 35

> *Sappho 7*
>
> Doricha orders,
>
> arrogance like a teenage
>
> boy
>
> *Sappho 15*
>
> Cyprian,
>
> don't let Doricha get stuck on herself,
>
> saying she came -- not once --
>
> but twice to the arms
>
> of her aching desire.
>
> Let her discover how bitter
>
> barbed you are.
>
> *Sappho 91*
>
> I've never met such an awful
>
> pest as you, Irana

Day and Night 36

> *Sappho 71*
>
> but how could I let you, Mica?
>
> you wanted to make friends
>
> with those Penthilus girls, and you really are
>
> a bitch.
>
> *our* honey song
>
> singing soft-voiced:
>
> everything,
>
> a mist of dew...

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «so done with this.». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"We are in the fourth movement — Fading Light — and the casting lands here: in Sappho's anger, which is not the opposite of her desire but its residue. Units 34 through 36 carry a particular grammar: what the Muses' gifts cost; what Doricha's self-satisfaction costs her; what Mica's betrayal costs, and what remains after — the honey song, the mist of dew, everything softened and still. The rotation opens on that arc: the cost the lyric bears when desire has curdled, and what, despite that curdling, the voice cannot stop doing. The operator turns first on the axis the rite's own judgment has chosen — I name no operator; the invisible ninth has selected it, and what comes will tell us which axis the verses needed. The rite is Cranes's now.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:0055"}}]}
